stem:

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate Rudo's capital at 1 January 2025.
parts.explanation: Assets: equipment 13,440, inventory 5,720, trade receivables 2,640, prepaid rent 495, bank 3,465 = 25,760. Liabilities: trade payables 5,260 and accruals 545 = 5,805. Capital 19,955.

parts.explanation: Receipts 71,245 less payments 60,315 less closing bank 6,150 = 4,780.
parts.workedSolution: 1. Receipts 71,245 less payments 60,315 less closing bank 6,150 = 4,780.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Calculate the total of depreciation and the change in the allowance for irrecoverable debts to be charged for the year.
parts.explanation: Depreciation 10% × 22,400 = 2,240; allowance 5% × 3,340 = 167, an increase of 27; total 2,267.
parts.workedSolution: 1. Depreciation 10% × 22,400 = 2,240; allowance 5% × 3,340 = 167, an increase of 27; total 2,267.

parts.label: (f)
parts.stem: Calculate the profit for the year.
parts.explanation: Revenue 69,440 - cost of sales 39,180 = gross profit 30,260; + discount received 555 - expenses 23,987 = 6,828.
parts.workedSolution: 1. Revenue 69,440 - cost of sales 39,180 = gross profit 30,260; + discount received 555 - expenses 23,987 = 6,828.

parts.label: (j)
parts.stem: Rudo says: "My business is healthy because profit is 6,828 and I drew 4,780." Evaluate her statement.

points.description: Profit for the year of 6,828 compared with revenue gives a profit margin of 9.83%, which supports her view
Drawings of 4,780 were less than profit, so capital grew
The profit depends on estimates and balancing figures from incomplete records, so she should keep full records before relying on it

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The profit margin of 9.83% and profit above drawings support her view. But the figures come from incomplete records with balancing items, so they are less reliable and she should keep full books.

parts.label: (j)
parts.stem: Sithole feels the agreement is unfair because Chikwava has invested more capital. Using the figures, evaluate the agreement.

points.description: Chikwava receives 12,061 against Sithole's 14,349, a difference that reflects his larger capital and 3/5 share
Sithole's salary and 2/5 share partly compensate him for working in the business
The agreement is fair if his work is valued at the salary; otherwise they could renegotiate the ratio or salary

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Chikwava receives US\$12,061 and Sithole US\$14,349. The larger share reflects Chikwava's capital, while Sithole's salary and share compensate him for his work. It is fair if the salary reflects his effort, otherwise they should renegotiate.

parts.explanation: One mark each for two reasoned points and a judgement.

hints: Prepare the statement of profit or loss first, then the appropriation account.
Fixed capitals: appropriations go through the current accounts.

stem: Dube and Ncube run a garden-supplies business in Gweru. They have no written agreement. Ncube lent the partnership US\$14,500 at the start of the year. Profit for the year ended 31 December 2025 before any interest on the loan was US\$41,765. Dube works full time and says he should receive a salary of US\$7,350; he also says interest should be allowed on capital at 6% (Dube US\$38,000, Ncube US\$22,000) and that residual profit should be shared 3 : 2. Ncube says the Partnership Act applies.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Decide whether each claim is supported by the Partnership Act when there is no agreement.

left.content: Dube's claim to 6% interest on capital
Dube's claim that profits are shared 3 : 2
Ncube's claim to interest on his loan

parts.explanation: The Act gives no salary, no interest on capital and equal sharing; a loan earns 5%.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the interest due to Ncube on his loan.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Calculate the profit each partner receives if the Act applies.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Calculate Dube's total profit if Dube's terms were agreed (salary, 6% interest and 3 : 2 sharing of the residual, after loan interest).
parts.explanation: Profit after loan interest 41,040; salary 7,350; interest 2,280 + 1,320; residual 30,090; Dube: 7,350 + 2,280 + 18,054 = 27,684.
parts.workedSolution: 1. Profit after loan interest 41,040; salary 7,350; interest 2,280 + 1,320; residual 30,090; Dube: 7,350 + 2,280 + 18,054 = 27,684.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Advise the partners how to resolve the disagreement and evaluate the effect on each of them.

points.description: Under the Act each receives 20,520; under Dube's terms he receives 27,684 and Ncube 13,356
Dube's terms recognise his work and larger capital, so may be fair, but Ncube loses a lot
The Act applies only if there is no agreement, so the partners can agree different terms
Advice: agree and sign a written partnership agreement with reasonable terms

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Under the Act each partner would receive US\$20,520, but under Dube's terms he receives US\$27,684 and Ncube US\$13,356. Dube's terms recognise his work and capital but are costly for Ncube. The partners should negotiate and sign a written agreement.

parts.explanation: One mark each; figures must be used.

explanation: This item tests the default rules of the Partnership Act and their effect on the appropriation of profit.
hints: Under the Act: equal shares, no salary, no interest on capital, 5% on loans.
The loan interest is an expense deducted before profit is shared.
